clue.text: A la minor player, first to miss in match when shoot-out occurs?

parts.note: à la means in the manner of, or after the style of
an extra is a bit-part actor in a film

indicators.note: the picked letter goes inside the word for a match

parts.note: a tie is a cup match

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word miss is the one taken

explanation.surface: A bit-part footballer is first to miss in a match decided on penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to' picks M from 'miss', which 'in' places inside TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A penalty shoot-out is held only once a drawn tie has gone through the added period of play, so the phrase gives its timing.

clue.text: Perhaps test leading attaché according to circumstances

parts.note: test, leading and attaché are each a word that can precede case (test case, leading case, attaché case), so each is perhaps whatever the case may be

explanation.surface: An exam perhaps leads a junior diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: The three words are a list of examples, each completing a familiar phrase with 'case'; the answer read literally describes them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is used to mean depending on which situation actually applies.

clue.text: Those guys briefly ahead of heavy drinker dropping first to last in race

indicators.note: ahead of means the first piece comes before the second
cut short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: those guys are they

indicators.note: the opening letter falls to the end of the word

parts.note: a soak is a drunkard

explanation.surface: Some blokes are ahead of a drunk who drops from first to last in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oaks is a classic flat race for fillies run at Epsom in England.

clue.text: Aaron's going crazy about hot meat dish for festival

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed around the other pieces
letters that go crazy are thrown into disorder

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
hash is a dish of chopped cooked meat

explanation.surface: Aaron goes mad over a hot meat dish served at a feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going crazy' turns AARONS into ROS ... ANA, and 'about' wraps that round H and HASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosh Hashana is the Jewish New Year celebration.

clue.text: Candour regularly shown after Times article reveals idyllic place

indicators.note: the selected letters come after the earlier pieces

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: every other letter of candour is taken

explanation.surface: Frankness in a newspaper article reveals a paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes ADU, the even letters of 'Candour'. 'Times' here is the multiplication sign, not the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanadu is Kubla Khan's pleasure dome in Coleridge's poem, now a byword for an idealised paradise.

clue.text: Calibrated again, having considered adjusting top mark

indicators.note: adjusting the position of one letter shifts it elsewhere in the word

parts.note: regarded means considered
A is the top grade awarded

explanation.surface: Someone recalibrated a scale after weighing up a change to the highest grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusting' moves the A of REGARDED one place along.
explanation.definitionFit: To regrade is to grade or calibrate anew, assigning fresh levels.

clue.text: 1ac initially knocked back drink

indicators.note: a drink knocked back suggests the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the initials of the 1 across phrase form the football abbreviation a.e.t.

explanation.surface: A drink knocked back at the start of extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' reverses AET, the standard scoreline abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a common hot beverage, a cuppa.

clue.text: Between terms, as might be equivalent to half of each?

parts.words: as might be equivalent to half of each
parts.note: the middle of the word year is EA, which is half of the word each

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what lies between terms, perhaps half of each.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the answer says take the middle of 'year': that gives EA, the first half of 'each'.
explanation.definitionFit: The summer holiday falls halfway through the calendar, between academic terms.

clue.text: Criminal racketeers harm subject of intensive questioning?

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are crooked, set wrongly

explanation.surface: Gangsters do harm to someone being interrogated.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: consumers are surveyed intensively by questionnaires.
explanation.definitionFit: Studies of buyers' preferences are built on asking many people many questions.

clue.text: Boy on run in 6 causing crime

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after
the letter goes inside the drink

parts.note: the answer to 6 down is a drink
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy running into a drink causes an offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country or sovereign.

clue.text: Old man's instrument missing number one and the final number

indicators.note: missing means these letters are left out

parts.note: a grand piano is a large keyboard instrument
I is the Roman numeral one
No is the abbreviation for number, here the one at the end

explanation.surface: An old man's piano is short of its finest and last pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops I from the middle and NO from the end of GRAND PIANO. The 's is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Old man is informal for a father, and by extension a grandfather is an older family patriarch.

clue.text: 23 circulated letter from overseas

indicators.note: sent round, so the word is turned back to front; the letters also sitting backwards inside this word are a coincidence

parts.note: the answer to 23 across is a past tense of eat

explanation.surface: A letter from abroad was circulated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulated' reverses ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet, foreign to English.

clue.text: Game in which evil character reportedly sneaked around

indicators.note: what is heard, not what is written

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the wicked alter ego of Dr Jekyll

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: In a game, a villain was said to have crept about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns SNEAKED into ANDSEEK.
explanation.definitionFit: Hide-and-seek is a children's game where one player looks for the others.

clue.text: Favourites cross over for each salesman

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upwards

parts.note: pets are favourites
a rood is a cross or crucifix
per means for each

explanation.surface: Popular choices change sides on behalf of every seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns PETS ROOD into DOORSTEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorstepper sells by calling at houses, standing on the step.

clue.text: Fine female donkey?

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
ess is the suffix marking a female, as in lioness

explanation.surface: A fine female donkey, the clue asks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whimsical coinage for a she-donkey hides a verb; the definition is a verb, to fine.
explanation.definitionFit: To levy a charge, tax or penalty on someone is one sense, close to fining them.

clue.text: Comrade put out by Trump's front?

definitions.text: Comrade put out by Trump's front?

indicators.note: by here means beside, so the opening letter sits next to the jumbled letters
letters put out are knocked out of place
the front of the word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A political ally is irritated by the Republican president's facade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges COMRADE; 'front' takes T from 'Trump's'. Read whole, the clue is a member of the rival party discomfited by Trump.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat belongs to the US party opposing Trump's Republicans, so naturally upset by his leadership.

clue.text: German units arresting extremely smart genius

indicators.note: arresting means holding inside

parts.note: ein is German for one, so two units are ein and ein

indicators.note: the extreme letters of the word smart

explanation.surface: German troops detain a very clever person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives ST from 'smart', which 'arresting' holds between the two EINs.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein's name is used for any brilliant person.

clue.text: City still over the moon

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
static means still, unmoving

explanation.surface: A city still celebrating.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the moon is an idiom for delighted, matching overjoyed.

clue.text: Sons left to enter empty, ostentatious display

indicators.note: the letter goes into the word for empty

parts.note: to purge is to empty or clear out

explanation.surface: Sons allowed into a vacant, showy event.
explanation.definitionFit: A splurge is a lavish, showy spree of spending.

clue.text: Audibly breathe deeply, vital for soul

indicators.note: the pieces are taken by sound, not spelling

parts.note: to sigh is to breathe out deeply; key means vital, essential

explanation.surface: Taking a deep breath is vital for the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human mind or spirit.

clue.text: Cove water in Calais — boater there?

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a chap
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A bay and water at a French port suggest a boatman.
explanation.walkthrough: A boater is a straw hat; 'there' points back to Calais, so the French word for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapeau is French for hat, and a boater is a kind of straw hat.

clue.text: Little bird needing energy to rise over the hill

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
sap means energy or vitality

explanation.surface: A small bird needs energy to fly over a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' turns TIT SAP upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms for being too old to perform well.

clue.text: Absence of commitment tends to creep into account towards the end

indicators.note: the word for tends creeps inside

parts.note: late means near the end
leans means tends or inclines

explanation.surface: A lack of obligation tends to sneak into the books near the deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to creep into' puts LEANS inside AC plus LATE, just after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting with nothing against one's name means no prior obligations or record.

clue.text: Put away 6 back to front

indicators.note: the back letter goes to the front

parts.note: the answer to 6 down is a drink

explanation.surface: Drink a sixth item, back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves the final A of TEA to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away food is idiomatic for consuming it, past tense here.

clue.text: Playfully resume chasing black cat?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters chase, coming after

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: the letters are toyed with into a new order

explanation.surface: A cat playfully resumes chasing a black cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playfully' turns RESUME into URMESE, which goes after B.
explanation.definitionFit: The Burmese is a breed of domestic cat, so cat with a question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Put away 23 back to front

indicators.note: the back letter goes to the front

parts.note: the answer to 23 across is a past tense of a verb

explanation.surface: Put away the earlier item, back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves the E at the end of ATE to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away food is idiomatic for consuming it.

clue.text: Cannabis returned with illegal drugs, the last used in an estate?

definitions.text: the last used in an estate?

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so reversed

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
gear is slang for illegal drugs

explanation.surface: Cannabis and other drugs were found in an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate here is an estate car; the highest gear is the last one engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest ratio in a gearbox is the final one a driver selects when accelerating.

clue.text: Finishing learning, then sick on Thursday

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after

parts.note: getting can mean understanding, grasping
rough means feeling ill

explanation.surface: Someone finishing school is ill on Thursday.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting through a task means completing it.
